correctness.rationale: For disjoint union the closure test is componentwise; for a join, a selected nonclique on either side forces the other side to be selected in full. The four possibilities by clique status are disjoint, and every mixed induced path has both nonadjacent endpoints in one side. This proves the two-polynomial recursion in both directions, with the empty and singleton cases explicit. On a supplied binary cotree convolution and all coefficient work at child sizes a,b cost O(ab), since a+b≤2ab and completeness is propagated by flags. The sum of ab counts each pair at its lowest common ancestor. For the coefficient claim, universal extension is K_H+zF_H; the connected cases at order five therefore come from exactly the nine admissible four-vertex types with the listed degree keys. For disconnected graphs of order at most five at most one component can be noncomplete, and binomial factors preserve its known smaller-order unimodality by the two-step difference test. Anti-exchange extends from connected components because an obstruction cannot use two different components. Independent replay `python3 /workspace/review_evidence/reproduce.py 1` compared direct forbidden triples with cotree polynomial calculations on all 535 labelled cographs through order five, counted 462 labelled trivially perfect graphs, verified the nine table rows, and found only the five labellings of the star nonunimodal. The direct star coefficient and cutoff calculations are correct as background.
residual_risks: The replay covers order at most five; the cotree argument proves the unbounded claim. The operation count assumes a supplied cotree and is not a bit-complexity estimate.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The two convexity notions agree on stars because the neighbors of any one vertex are pairwise nonadjacent. The polynomial and its elementary cutoff inequalities are therefore a mechanical consequence of earlier counting, not a separate contribution. Neither this implication nor the scalar star total addresses whether other trivially perfect types at order five are nonunimodal.

originality.rationale: PASS for the narrowed induced-path cotree recurrence and smallest-order uniqueness claim. The repaired document credits the specialization explicitly, keeping those facts only as background. No earlier inspected statement or mechanical implication subsumes the full cograph recurrence under the induced convention or the comparison across all five-vertex trivially perfect types.
residual_risks: Earlier equivalent closure-polynomial formulas, possibly under bounded-width or induced convexity terminology, remain possible.

value.rationale: The recurrence evaluates the full distribution of a natural graph closure, including both coefficients and shape rather than merely the total. It supplies exact polynomial arithmetic in a standard graph decomposition. The smallest-order uniqueness result is a structurally meaningful obstruction to unimodality in the associated convex-geometric class and excludes alternative minimal examples. The elementary star calculation by itself is not counted as a valuable new contribution.
residual_risks: No consequence is claimed for unimodality of arbitrary convex geometries or beyond the stated smallest-order classification.
